solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Luke possibly seen with Mike penning American hymns (6,5)

indicatorNotes.penning: to pen something is to shut it in, so MIC holds US

blocks.note: Luke is one of the four Gospels; 'possibly' marks him as an example
a mike is a microphone, MIC for short

annotation.surface: Someone named Luke joins a man called Mike to write songs of praise.
annotation.walkthrough: Mike reads as a man's name, or as the NATO letter M, but here it is the microphone, spelt MIC.
annotation.definitionFit: Gospel music is the tradition of Christian hymns and spirituals.

entries.clue: Rats on plants (7)

blocks.note: to rat on someone is to grass, British slang for informing to the police
a botanical family: meadow and lawn plants

annotation.surface: Rodents sitting on the greenery.
annotation.walkthrough: Rats looks like a noun, the animals; it is a verb, informs. In British slang a grass is an informer.
annotation.definitionFit: He rats and he grasses both mean he informs; grasses are also a family of plants.

entries.clue: Spooner’s demand for payment, perhaps, when this puzzle appears? (6)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: a dun is a demand for payment; 'perhaps' = SAY; swap the D and S sounds

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a bill might land on the day this crossword runs.
annotation.walkthrough: SAY is the usual stand-in for 'perhaps' or 'for example'. The definition is a self-reference: this puzzle ran in the Sunday Telegraph.
annotation.definitionFit: A self-referential definition: this toughie ran in the Sunday Telegraph, so the day it appears names the answer.

entries.clue: Blunder in foreign articles by Bush (10)

indicatorNotes.in: ERR sits in BY, as a blunder sits in a text

blocks.note: EL is Spanish for 'the', DER German

annotation.surface: A gaffe in foreign papers written by a US president.
annotation.walkthrough: Bush looks like George W. Bush at the end of a news story about a gaffe; it is the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: The elderberry is a shrub, a bush bearing clusters of dark berries.

entries.clue: What makes it hard to see half of oversights (4)

annotation.definition: What makes it hard to see

indicatorNotes.half of: keep only the first half of the word

blocks.note: oversights = MISTAKES; its first four letters

annotation.surface: A remark on what causes oversights.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a comment about oversights, which are mistakes; halving MISTAKES leaves MIST.
annotation.definitionFit: Mist cuts visibility, making it hard to see.

entries.clue: Voters upset about Independent newspaper’s back page that’s outdated? (8)

indicatorNotes.upset: the letters are knocked out of order
indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged letters go around I

blocks.note: last letter of newspaper, also fodder

annotation.surface: Readers revolt over a stale back page in The Independent.
annotation.walkthrough: Independent and newspaper suggest The Independent and its back page; the definition is 'page', a servant, not a sheet of paper.
annotation.definitionFit: A servitor is an old word for a servant or attendant, and a page is a young servant.

entries.clue: Bends stick broken by Roman here (7)

indicatorNotes.broken by: CANE is split open and HIC put in

blocks.note: a cane is a walking stick

annotation.surface: Someone bends a stick, and a Roman breaks it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roman here' means the word a Roman would use for 'here'.
annotation.definitionFit: A chicane is a pair of tight bends put into a racetrack or road to slow traffic.

entries.clue: Tired, ran away (7)

blocks.note: as water flows off a sink or field

annotation.surface: Someone worn out who ran off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ran away' suggests a fugitive, but it is liquid running off.
annotation.definitionFit: Drained means exhausted, and liquid that drained ran away.

entries.clue: Unpleasant death drew on, making you unhappy (11)

indicatorNotes.Unpleasant: the letters are put into a nasty, disordered state

annotation.surface: A grim death approached, and that saddens you.
annotation.walkthrough: Unpleasant reads as describing the death; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone downhearted has lost heart, which is to be unhappy.

entries.clue: Portion proving sufficient (7)

blocks.note: a helping of food on a plate
something that serves is enough for the purpose

annotation.surface: A helping that turns out to be enough.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses sit so close that the clue reads as one idea, a plateful that fills you up.
annotation.definitionFit: A serving is a portion; 'that will serve' means that will do.

entries.clue: Excuse warmth, we hear one might be in a tent (11)

annotation.definition: one might be in a tent

indicatorNotes.we hear: asks for the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: grounds = excuse, as in grounds for complaint; heat = warmth

annotation.surface: Pleading a spell of warm weather as a reason to camp.
annotation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'grounds heat' runs into 'ground sheet'; the word break moves.
annotation.definitionFit: A groundsheet is the waterproof sheet laid on the floor of a tent.

entries.clue: Ernie right to probe one smart Alick (8)

indicatorNotes.to probe: a probe pushes inside something, so R pushes into ACE

blocks.note: Ernie Wise, of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise
an ace counts as one in cards

annotation.surface: A comic named Ernie pushing a know-all into line.
annotation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was the straight man of Morecambe and Wise, the best-loved British comedy duo of the 1970s.
annotation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who thinks they know it all, a smart alec.

entries.clue: Fearsome type of bream regularly seen in port (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly means at even intervals, so take every second letter
indicatorNotes.seen in: something seen in a port is inside it, so RA sits within VIGO

blocks.note: Vigo, a port in north-west Spain
second and fourth letters of bREaM... b-R-e-A-m

annotation.surface: A frightening kind of fish turns up in the harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Type of bream' suggests a fish species, but 'Fearsome type' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, fierce woman.

entries.clue: Ultra harsh after trashing valedictory performance (4,6)

indicatorNotes.trashing: wrecking the phrase so its letters can be rebuilt

annotation.surface: Critics savaged a farewell show.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as a verdict on a bad review; the two words are simply letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A last hurrah is a final appearance or effort before retirement, a farewell performance.

entries.clue: Pack present (4)

blocks.note: to front a TV show or party

annotation.surface: An instruction to wrap a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pack present' reads as wrapping a gift; both words switch roles, a noun for a crowd and a verb for fronting a show.
annotation.definitionFit: A host of people is a large pack; to host a programme is to present it.

entries.clue: Knives Out politician welcomes partner back on shift (3,1,4,2)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: a host welcomes guests inside, so GOVE takes ETAM in
indicatorNotes.back: back means backwards, so MATE is written in reverse

blocks.note: Michael Gove, the British politician who knifed Boris Johnson's 2016 leadership bid

annotation.surface: A politician from the film Knives Out takes his partner back.
annotation.walkthrough: Knives Out is a murder-mystery film, but here it is the knives out for a rival: Gove turned on his ally Johnson in 2016.
annotation.definitionFit: Get a move on means hurry up; shift is British slang for going fast.

entries.clue: Every two years, good American seen to be in love (8)

indicatorNotes.seen to be in: something in love is inside the word for love, so A sits within NIL

blocks.note: bien is French for well or good
love is a score of nothing

annotation.surface: A decent American falls for someone once every other year.
annotation.walkthrough: BIEN is foreign with no flag in the clue, so it has to be spotted from the crossing letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Latin bi- (two) and annus (year) build the sense of once every two years.

entries.clue: Identify brave person shouting when out of the news – ultimately, he should be better (10)

indicatorNotes.out of: out of means lacking, so the Ns are missing from each word
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the final letter of he

blocks.note: the news read as N’s, plural of N for new: the Ns to strip out

annotation.surface: Naming a hero who kept quiet in the press, saying he ought to improve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The news' stands for the plural of N, the abbreviation for new: every N comes out of NAME, LION and RANT.
annotation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to make or become better, the verb 'better'.

entries.clue: Funny remark from glutton that’s tucked into English butter (7)

indicatorNotes.tucked into: food is tucked into a mouth, so PIG goes inside E + RAM

blocks.note: a greedy eater is a pig
a ram butts with its head: something that butts

annotation.surface: A quip about a greedy eater tucking into English butter.
annotation.walkthrough: Butter is the dairy spread in the surface, and a glutton tucking in fits; it is really 'one who butts'.
annotation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty saying.

entries.clue: Cost not large as will stock book (4)

indicatorNotes.not: not says the large part is absent, so OS comes out of COST
indicatorNotes.will stock: AS holds CT as a shop holds goods

annotation.surface: The cost of a small item, as a bookshop keeps a book in stock.
annotation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is the clothing-size abbreviation for large.
annotation.definitionFit: Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament.

entries.clue: Fancy that chap entering fancy race (7)

indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go inside, so HIM goes into the rearranged RACE
indicatorNotes.fancy: the letters of RACE are rearranged

annotation.surface: Surprise at a man entering a fancy-dress race.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'fancy' does two jobs: the first is the definition, a noun meaning an illusion; the second rearranges RACE.
annotation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fancy, an illusion of the mind.

entries.clue: Spoke with artist apparently confined to bed? (6)

indicatorNotes.apparently: flags that 'confined to bed' is to be read as LAID UP, with up turning LAID round in a down entry

blocks.note: confined to bed = laid up, so LAID written upwards

annotation.surface: Talking with a painter who is laid up in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: Spoke looks like the past tense of speak; it is the wheel spoke. 'Laid up' means ill in bed, and read literally in a down clue it sends LAID upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A radial is a line or part running out from a centre, as a spoke does.

entries.clue: Group of three taking air around centre of Zürich (6)

annotation.definitionNote: TRIUNE is usually an adjective, three in one; the clue uses it as a noun

indicatorNotes.taking: taking means taking in, so TUNE holds RI
indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so TUNE wraps RI
indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre of a word is its middle letters, RI in a six-letter Zurich

annotation.surface: A trio gasping for breath in the middle of Zurich.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking air' suggests breathing; air is a tune.
annotation.definitionFit: A theological term: triune describes the Trinity, three in one, stretched here to mean a group of three.

entries.clue: Tense and excited about lead track being laid down (3,5)

indicatorNotes.about: about means turned around, so T + UP is reversed

blocks.note: the A-side is the main track of a single

annotation.surface: Nervous and thrilled as the lead song is recorded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Laid down' suggests recording a track in the studio; it means stored away.
annotation.definitionFit: Put aside and laid down both mean saved for later, as wine is laid down.

entries.clue: Feature of short service (4)

indicatorNotes.short: short means cut off, so CHINA loses its tail

blocks.note: CHINA, a dinner service, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Something that marks a quick church service.
annotation.walkthrough: Service suggests a church or a tennis serve; it is a set of china.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the chin is one of the features of a face.

entries.clue: Rather like oil devotee? (7)

blocks.note: derv is British for diesel fuel

annotation.surface: A question about someone keen on fuel.
annotation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel for road vehicles, so 'derv-ish' is somewhat like oil.
annotation.definitionFit: A dervish is a member of a Sufi religious order, a devotee.

entries.clue: Frenchman’s really chucking out very old clothes (7)

indicatorNotes.chucking out: chucking out means ejecting, so V is thrown out of VRAIMENT

annotation.surface: A Frenchman genuinely throwing away very old clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very old clothes' reads as one phrase; 'very' belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'old clothes' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for clothing.

entries.clue: Call home in a terribly miserable state (11)

blocks.note: anagram of CALL HOME IN A

annotation.surface: Phoning home while deeply unhappy.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram runs across four words, and 'terribly' seems to go with 'miserable'.
annotation.definitionFit: A clinical name: melancholia was the old medical term for deep depression, a miserable state.
